findings.issue_text: [High/bug] ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException, but AdminPermissions.registerListener — gated on Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ), i.e. exactly when the V2 evaluator is active — calls clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false) on every ClientRemovedEvent; every client deletion under the feature hits an exception in the event listener, either failing the delete request or silently skipping cleanup, and since V2 has no other cleanup path, per-client authorization resources and their permissions are orphaned in the DB forever.

[Medium/bug] canMapRoles, canMapCompositeRoles and canMapClientScopeRoles in ClientPermissionsV2 do not check root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.MANAGE_CLIENTS) (nor treat a MANAGE grant as implying map-roles), unlike canManage/canView/canConfigure in the same class; under V2, an admin holding the manage-clients role — including master-realm admins, for whom isAdminSameRealm() is false so hasPermission(...) always returns false — is denied role mapping unless a separate fine-grained permission exists, a behavior regression vs V1 and internally inconsistent.

[Medium/bug] canExchangeTo throws UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2"); token-exchange flows consult this evaluator, so with the feature enabled a token-exchange request surfaces as a 500 error instead of being allowed or denied — throwing from a permission check invoked during request processing is not a safe stub and should at minimum deny (or the calling path must be feature-gated).

[Medium/bug] getClientsWithPermission: resourceStore.findByType(server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...) also returns the "Clients" type resource itself, so when a type-level (all-clients) permission is granted, hasGrantedPermission evaluates true and granted.add(resource.getName()) adds the literal string "Clients" — a bogus entry that is not a client ID — to the returned set of client IDs, while the method has no way to convey "all clients" semantics for type-level grants.

[Low/doc_defect] The javadoc for requireView() and requireViewClientScopes() in ClientPermissionEvaluator says "Returns {@code true} if ...", but these are void methods that throw ForbiddenException; the docs should read "Throws ForbiddenException if ... returns false" like the other require* methods.

[Low/concurrency] The hasPermission(ClientModel, String) fallback path calls AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...), a get-or-create invoked from a read-only can* check — GET requests therefore trigger persistent DB writes, concurrent first requests can race to create the type resource, and it is inconsistent with hasPermission(String scope), which returns false without creating anything when the type resource is absent.

[Low/bug] Dead code in ClientPermissionsV2: getEvaluationContext(...) is never called (its only plausible caller, canExchangeTo, throws), the logger field is never used, and the static import of AdminPermissionManagement.TOKEN_EXCHANGE is unused (along with the ClientModelIdentity/DefaultEvaluationContext/EvaluationContext/AccessToken imports it alone justifies).

[Low/performance] getClientsWithPermission runs a full policy evaluation (root.evaluatePermission) per resource of type "Clients", i.e. O(n) complete evaluations per call, making every call that uses it (e.g. filtered client listing) expensive for realms with many per-client permissions; a single evaluation over the resource set or per-request caching should be considered.

[Low/test_gap] The new MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE scope / canMapClientScopeRoles path is never exercised in PermissionClientTest — the scope isn't even imported in the test and no test maps roles to a client scope.

[Low/test_gap] No test in PermissionClientTest deletes a client that has a per-client permission/resource and verifies the authorization data is cleaned up; such a test would have caught the setPermissionsEnabled breakage.

goldens.comment: Inconsistent feature flag bug causing orphaned permissions. The AdminPermissions event listener, responsible for cleaning up permissions upon role, client, or group removal, is incorrectly guarded by the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) feature flag. This is inconsistent with other methods in the class that use ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2. Consequently, if ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled but V1 is not, the permission cleanup logic will not execute, leading to orphaned permission data. Cleanup should occur regardless of which fine-grained authorization version is enabled.

In hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope), the resource lookup uses findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId()), but AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource creates per-client resources with the owner set to resourceServer.getClientId(), so this lookup will never find those resources and will always fall back to the 'all-clients' resource, effectively ignoring client-specific permissions.

In getClientsWithPermission(String scope), iterating resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and returning resource.getName() will only ever consider the type-level 'Clients' resource (per-client resources have no type) and return its name, while AvailableRoleMappingResource#getRoleIdsWithPermissions expects actual client IDs to pass to realm.getClientById, which can lead to incorrect behavior or a null client and subsequent failures.

In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, the method getResourceTypeResource could return null, leading to a NullPointerException in findByResource. Defensive null checks are needed to prevent this issue.
Remove unused getEvaluationContext private method in ClientPermissionsV2 - it is defined but never called

adjudication_records.issue_text: [High/bug] ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException, but AdminPermissions.registerListener — gated on Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ), i.e. exactly when the V2 evaluator is active — calls clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false) on every ClientRemovedEvent; every client deletion under the feature hits an exception in the event listener, either failing the delete request or silently skipping cleanup, and since V2 has no other cleanup path, per-client authorization resources and their permissions are orphaned in the DB forever.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `AdminPermissions.registerListener` is now gated on `Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)` and, when enabled, it handles `ClientModel.ClientRemovedEvent` by calling `management(session, realm).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false)`. The diff also introduces `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()` returning `ClientPermissionsV2`, whose `setPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel, boolean)` explicitly throws `UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2")`. If the V2 management path is used under this feature (implied by the V2 additions and the listener’s new feature gate), client removal will trigger an exception in the event listener.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] canMapRoles, canMapCompositeRoles and canMapClientScopeRoles in ClientPermissionsV2 do not check root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.MANAGE_CLIENTS) (nor treat a MANAGE grant as implying map-roles), unlike canManage/canView/canConfigure in the same class; under V2, an admin holding the manage-clients role — including master-realm admins, for whom isAdminSameRealm() is false so hasPermission(...) always returns false — is denied role mapping unless a separate fine-grained permission exists, a behavior regression vs V1 and internally inconsistent.

adjudication.rationale: In `ClientPermissionsV2`, `canMapRoles(ClientModel)`, `canMapCompositeRoles(ClientModel)`, and `canMapClientScopeRoles(ClientModel)` are implemented as `return hasPermission(client, ...)` only. The helper `hasPermission(...)` hard-denies when `!root.isAdminSameRealm()` (`if (!root.isAdminSameRealm()) { return false; }`), and these map-roles methods do not have any bypass like `root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.MANAGE_CLIENTS)` (which *is* used in `canManage(ClientModel)`, `canManageClientScopes()`, etc.). As a result, callers who rely on admin roles (e.g., MANAGE_CLIENTS, and especially cross-realm/admin scenarios where `isAdminSameRealm()` is false) can be denied role-mapping operations unless an explicit fine-grained permission exists, while other client operations still succeed via the admin-role checks. This inconsistency is directly observable from the diff and can lead to broken/changed authorization behavior under V2.

While the diff does not show the token-exchange request path invoking these methods (so a concrete 500 during token exchange is not directly provable here), throwing from an evaluator implementation is a risky/incomplete stub unless all calling paths are feature-gated or guaranteed not to call these methods in V2.

adjudication.rationale: In `ClientPermissionEvaluator`, the new Javadocs for `requireView()` and `requireViewClientScopes()` state "Returns {@code true} if ...", but both methods are declared `void` and are intended to throw `ForbiddenException` when the corresponding `can*` check fails (as correctly documented for other `require*` methods in the same interface). This is a diff-verifiable documentation inconsistency, not a runtime bug.

adjudication.rationale: In `ClientPermissionsV2#hasPermission(ClientModel, String)`, when the per-client `Resource` is missing it falls back to `AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE)` (new code in this diff). By contrast, `hasPermission(String)` simply `findByName(...)` and returns `false` if the type resource doesn’t exist. That inconsistency is verifiable from the diff and can introduce unwanted side-effects during `can*` checks depending on whether `getResourceTypeResource` is a get-or-create API (the diff doesn’t show its implementation, so the “persistent DB writes / races” part can’t be proven here).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/performance] getClientsWithPermission runs a full policy evaluation (root.evaluatePermission) per resource of type "Clients", i.e. O(n) complete evaluations per call, making every call that uses it (e.g. filtered client listing) expensive for realms with many per-client permissions; a single evaluation over the resource set or per-request caching should be considered.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `ClientPermissionsV2#getClientsWithPermission(String scope)`, it iterates over every resource of type `AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE` via `resourceStore.findByType(...)` and for each resource calls `hasGrantedPermission(resource, scope)`. That helper performs `root.evaluatePermission(new ResourcePermission(resource, resource.getScopes(), server), server)` per resource, implying O(N) full permission evaluations per call when there are many client resources. This is a concrete performance/scalability concern introduced by the diff, not a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/test_gap] The new MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE scope / canMapClientScopeRoles path is never exercised in PermissionClientTest — the scope isn't even imported in the test and no test maps roles to a client scope.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new client permission scope `MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE` (in `AdminPermissionsSchema`) and a new evaluator path `ClientPermissionsV2.canMapClientScopeRoles(...)` that checks that scope. In `PermissionClientTest`, the static imports include `MAP_ROLES` and `MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE` but not `MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE`, and the only role-mapping test (`testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient`) grants scopes `Set.of(MAP_ROLES, MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE, CONFIGURE)` and exercises user role mapping and composite role creation—there is no test exercising mapping roles to a *client scope* or granting/evaluating `MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE`. This is a concrete missing-test issue for newly added nontrivial authorization logic, not a runtime defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/test_gap] No test in PermissionClientTest deletes a client that has a per-client permission/resource and verifies the authorization data is cleaned up; such a test would have caught the setPermissionsEnabled breakage.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds client-scoped permission evaluation logic via `ClientPermissionsV2` and extends the admin permissions schema with a `CLIENTS` resource type/scopes. `PermissionClientTest` adds several new tests (manage/configure/view/map-roles) that create per-client permissions (e.g., `createPermission(client, myclient.getId(), clientsType, Set.of(MANAGE), ...)`) but none delete a client that has such a per-client permission/resource and then assert that associated authorization data (resources/permissions/policies) is cleaned up. Given the new/changed removal listener logic in `AdminPermissions.registerListener` for `ClientRemovedEvent`, a deletion/cleanup regression would not be caught by the current tests, so this is a concrete, diff-grounded test gap rather than a confirmed runtime bug.
